title: Three Months and One Short Stamp
subtitle: 责任担当 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 责任担当（做人与做事·责任与担当）
meta: 主题语境：责任担当（做人与做事·责任与担当）　|　核心词汇：mission　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 mission 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1952 the clerk ① accepted the mission that no applicant in the office would have measured, and he said the accepting was the whole of the month. The ② mission, meaning the task itself and not the stamp, ran three months and stayed unmeasured in the book; a mission, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ mission in that office had the same short stamp beside it, and the ④ mission at the far counter, meaning the form they kept for the children to sign and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A mission, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the clerk said the measuring is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the mission was the whole of the matter, meaning the duty and not the task. The ⑥ mission, meaning the duty and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; mission, he said, is either something you accept or the only word that means both a task and a duty. He said the duty is the part they remember.

By 1957 the ⑦ mission had become a line in a file, and the file had become an argument about the short stamp. The ⑧ mission of the whole thing, the clerk wrote in May, was one office and three months of measuring; mission, he said, is either the form at the far counter or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ mission I remember is the task measured in the file, which closed in 1959 and is still measured as the quietest in the office. A ⑩ mission, my mother said in 1961, is the only task that improves by being measured; every mission, she said, is a duty that has agreed to look like a task. She said the duty was the honest half.

task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。

F. n. 使命；任务（指卷宗里写到、被测量的那一项）
G. n. 使命、天职（指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: accept the mission 意为“接受这一项使命”，1952 年那位书记员把办事处里没有一位申请人肯测量的一项使命做了一遍。
mission 意为“使命；任务”，指那项使命本身而不是小小的印章，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被测量。
mission 意为“使命；任务”，指办事处里每一项旁边的那一项，每一项旁边都有同一枚小小的印章。
mission 意为“使命；任务”，指最远那个窗口的留给孩子们签的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
mission 意为“使命、天职”，指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这项天职就是那件事的全部。
mission 意为“天职”，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西而不是那项使命，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
mission 意为“使命；任务”，指卷宗里写到、被测量的那一项，到 1957 年这一项成了卷宗里的一行。
mission 意为“使命之事”，书记员五月写道，整件事的使命之事是一处办事处和三个月份的测量。
mission 意为“使命；任务”，我记得的是卷宗里测量过的那一项，1959 年办结了，至今仍被说成办事处里最安静的一项。
mission 为抽象总称，母亲 1961 年说，使命是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的使命。
